stories.new_fact: Reuters reported that several large and mid-sized U.S. banks are narrowing permissions around internally developed AI agents after containment concerns at technology firms.
stories.new_takeaway: The relevant banking decision is whether an agent can be contained and essential operations continued, not whether a bank has announced an agent.
stories.why_now: The reported control tightening is dated November 23.
stories.previous_coverage: November 22 and 23 covered customer-delegated third-party account agents; this is a distinct internal-agent control response and continuity question.
stories.uncertainty: The reporting does not name banks or disclose control effectiveness, incident counts, or customer outcomes.
stories.watch: Named policies, tested recovery results, regulator findings, or agent permission and exception metrics.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added a lane-eight fresh reporting row for internal-agent permission tightening and continuity testing; evidence remains reporting, with no disclosed outcome metric.

stories.new_fact: OpenAI's November 23 release notes say GPT-6.2 in ChatGPT's chat tab is being rolled out to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers and report a 71.7 percent image-understanding score versus 47.4 percent for GPT-6 in its test.
stories.new_takeaway: The access change supports a controlled multimodal comparison, while the benchmark remains a lab-reported result rather than evidence of regulated-workflow accuracy.
stories.why_now: The release note is dated November 23.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol access; this is a different product surface and a newly disclosed image-understanding comparison.
stories.uncertainty: The release note does not supply bank-document error rates, test-set composition, or independent replication.
stories.watch: Rollout availability, task-specific independent evaluation, and revised model documentation.
